summary: Six direction samples written (hull a metal, b cinema, c weight; gear a machinery, b cinema, c dark but clear). Each is built from layers set as shares of the energy and then levelled; all six pass the build's hard rules, the new tests and every numeric target of the brief that I measured. Hull and gear families are levelled to equal integrated loudness. CLAP likes only hull_c; hull a and b score closest to 'taut plastic foil' (broadband noise crack and spray), gear a and c to 'cheap electronic beep' (the whine). I cannot hear; character judgements below are from spectrograms and numbers only.

sounds.layers: All from one event. (1) crack: white noise 1-8 kHz, onset 0.25 ms rise, T60 20 ms, 25 % of energy; plus a duller 1.8-5 kHz layer 3 ms later, 2 %. (2) plate: 22 inharmonic partials 180 Hz to about 4.9 kHz (ratios 1 to 27 over 180 Hz, random +-1.5 %), each a detuned pair (0.2-0.8 %, second member 0.55-0.9 of the first), pitch wander +-0.07 %, T60 2.4 s at 200 Hz falling as (200/f)^0.85 (0.17 s at 4 kHz), 54 %. (3) sub thump 72 falling to 44 Hz, 5.5 ms rise, T60 0.42 s, starts 2 ms after the crack, 25 %. (4) low body noise 90-400 Hz, 1 %. (5) three runs of 11, 14 and 9 uneven noise knocks at 1.5-5 kHz starting at 62, 105 and 170 ms, 1.2 %. Shares are of layer energy before normalisation, so the crack is the loudest moment but only the plate and sub carry the file's energy.
sounds.measured: Attack (30 ms): centre 2775 Hz (>=2500), 61.6 % above 1 kHz (>=60). Whole file: 42.5 % above 1 kHz (20-45), 23.2 % below 125 Hz (>=20), largest octave band 17.2 % (<=40). Ring: 150-1000 Hz band is -58 dBFS RMS at 0.8-1.0 s (peak -1.2 dBFS), so the 200 Hz line rings the whole 1.6 s in the spectrogram but the ring is faint at 0.8 s; strongest spectral peak 22.5 % at 52.7 Hz (the sub). Onset 0.02 ms, last 10 ms -90 dBFS. 1.6 s, one channel, true peak -1.2 dBFS (highest of the family, see levels), -31.0 LUFS.
sounds.unsure: (1) Whether it reads as metal or as a bell/bowl: the spectrogram shows a clean comb of low partial lines at 180-700 Hz that ring the longest, and the upper partials die within about 0.2 s as the brief asked, so the long part of the ring is low and tonal. (2) CLAP scores the crack as 'tapping on a taut plastic foil' (0.11-0.14) above 'steel plate clang' (0.01-0.05); removing the noise crack lowered the foil score, adding a modal 'tink' of short 1.6-8 kHz partials did not help (CLAP differences between variants were within its noise). I kept the noise crack because the brief asked for broadband. (3) Ring at 0.8 s is faint (-58 dBFS RMS); if the owner finds it too short, raise the plate share or lengthen the high partials. (4) The sub only comes after a 5.5 ms rise (needed to keep the attack above 60 % high-frequency); 2 ms after the crack it starts, the peak of the sub is about 6-8 ms late.

sounds.layers: Two channels built with synth.mid_side. Mid: sub drop 80 falling to 35 Hz (tau 0.28 s, 4 ms rise, 0.25 s hold, T60 1.5 s) 30 %; chest sine 140 falling to 70 Hz (T60 0.45 s) 7 %; crunch A, noise 300-3000 Hz, 1.5 ms rise, full level for 50 ms then T60 0.11 s (about 0.12 s audible), driven through tanh(3.5 x) and re-filtered 260-3600 Hz, 34 %; debris grains (360 grains of 1.5-6 ms noise, centres log-uniform 2-9 kHz, density exp(-t/0.38 s) over 1.15 s starting at 12 ms, amplitude falling with time) 4.5 %; a 12 ms click 2.5-9 kHz 1 %. Side: crunch B (other seed, same saturation) 22 %, the same grains weighted by random pan (-1..1) 3.5 %, click 0.8 %. Side is high-passed at 170 Hz by mid_side, so bass is identical in both channels.
sounds.measured: Below 125 Hz 42.8 % (>=30), 250 Hz-2 kHz 29.3 % (>=25; 250-500 2.2 + 500-1k 9.1 + 1-2k 18.0), above 2 kHz 22.6 % (>=8). Sub drop: 20-90 Hz band is -34 dBFS RMS at 0-0.2 s and still -58 at 0.8 s and -74 at 1.2 s (the pitch line is visible 35-80 Hz to about 1.3 s, well past 0.5 s). Channel correlation 0.49 (0.3-0.9), left/right level difference 0.20 dB, correlation below 150 Hz 1.0000. Mono sum is exactly the mid. 2.0 s, true peak -11.1 dBFS, -31.0 LUFS.
sounds.unsure: (1) It is the brightest of the three hit variants: 40.6 % above 1 kHz, mostly crunch harmonics and debris; the 'taut foil' similarity in CLAP (best neg, margin -0.06) probably comes from the dense noise. (2) Strongest spectral peak is 47.6 % at 52.7 Hz, which is a boom, but the brief's 'single peak' warning concerns resonances; the sub is a gliding sine, not a ringing mode. (3) One stray debris grain sits at about 1.05 s and is visible as a lone streak at 2-5 kHz in the spectrogram; might read as a tink. (4) The sounds ends audibly at about 1.3 s; the last 0.7 s of the 2.0 s file are nearly silent (sub below -80 dB). (5) Peak -11.1 dBFS looks low next to hull a at -1.2; it follows the LUFS rule, but the sub is under-weighted by K-weighting, so b may sound louder than the number says.

sounds.layers: One channel. Boom A: sine 78 falling to 50 Hz (tau 0.20 s, 1.2 % wobble, 6 ms rise, T60 1.9 s) 30 %; boom B: 52 falling to 34 Hz (tau 0.35 s, 1.5 % wobble, 8 ms rise, T60 2.3 s) 24 %; rumble: noise 25-95 Hz, T60 1.7 s, 8 %; body: broad noise 110-600 Hz (Butterworth order 2 band-pass, no resonance), 3 ms rise, T60 0.55 s, 34 %; soft knock: noise 0.8-2 kHz, 30 ms, T60 12 ms, 0.5 %.
sounds.measured: Below 125 Hz 59.4 % (>=50), below 60 Hz 33.8 % (>=15), octave bands above 125 Hz: 125-250 9.6, 250-500 19.1, 500-1k 9.8 (max 19.1 <= 25), above 1 kHz 2.1 % (<=3), attack 11.6 % above 800 Hz (5-20). Low tail: 20-125 Hz band -45 dBFS RMS at 0.8 s, -55 at 1.2 s, -61 at 1.4 s (peak -7.0). Strongest spectral peak 52 % at 46.9 Hz, which is the intended boom. 2.0 s, true peak -7.0 dBFS, -31.0 LUFS. CLAP: best match 'a deep heavy boom felt through a large metal structure', margin +0.16 (the only one of the six that passes).
sounds.unsure: Only an ear can say whether depth plus a broad body cures the plastic container; the approved Kenney boom had 67 % at 60-125 Hz and nothing above 1 kHz, this one has less 60-125 Hz (25 %) but more body at 125-600 Hz (about 38 %) and a knock. The sub lines are almost horizontal after 0.6 s (1.2-1.5 % wobble only); the long tail is deep rather than varied. It starts at 78 Hz and settles near 50 Hz, so on small loudspeakers without bass it leaves the body (125-600 Hz, 38 % of the energy) and the knock.

sounds.layers: One channel, all in one sequence. Motor whine: fundamental rises 180 to 420 Hz over 0.85 s (smoothstep) and holds, +-1.2 % wobble at 4.5 and 7.3 Hz plus a slow random drift, eight harmonics (levels 1, .75, .62, .42, .34, .22, .16, .10) each with its own slow level wobble, starts at 0 with an 8 ms rise, winds down over the last 120 ms before the lock; gear-train ratchet as uneven amplitude dips (about 29 per second, depth 55 %); second weaker whine 1.2 % off (harmonics 1, 3, 5) so the two beat; tooth ticks (noise 1.4-4.2 kHz, 1.5-4 ms, about 31 per second, uneven in time and level, swell in and out) and a faint air layer; shares of energy: whine 26 %, second whine 5 %, teeth 10 %, air 1 %. Lock at 1.80 s: clack (noise 2.2-9 kHz, T60 11 ms) 7.5 % plus three short rings at 2.63, 3.47 and 4.31 kHz (T60 45 ms) 2.5 %; 60 ms later (1.86 s) the clunk: body noise 100-400 Hz (T60 0.12 s) 14 %, sub 82 falling to 52 Hz (T60 0.24 s) 20 %, four resonances at 133, 187, 254 and 371 Hz with T60 0.30, 0.26, 0.22 and 0.16 s, 8 %.
sounds.measured: Above 1 kHz 32.8 % (15-40). Spectrogram and measure.py show the fundamental rising from 180 to about 420 Hz and holding with harmonics at 845, 1269, 1691 and 2103 Hz visible. Lock: first 30 ms centre 6507 Hz (>=2500); clunk 60 ms after the clack; in the 300 ms after the clack 29.6 % below 80 Hz, 33.5 % at 80-250 Hz. Ring: 1-6 kHz band falls from -32 to -56 dBFS in 100 ms; the low ring (133-371 Hz) lasts about 0.3 s. Onset 3.7 ms, last 10 ms -95.7 dBFS. 2.4 s, true peak -6.3 dBFS, -35.0 LUFS.
sounds.unsure: (1) The tooth ticks show as broadband vertical streaks up to 10 kHz in the spectrogram (noise ticks of 1.5-4 ms are wide); they could sound like a hissy rattle or crackle instead of gears, and could be mistaken for the 'crackle' he heard. (2) The whine holds at 420 Hz for about 1 s with only 1.2 % wobble; it could sound like a tone. (3) CLAP calls it 'a cheap electronic beep' (margin -0.05). (4) A sub (82 to 52 Hz) with no strong peak elsewhere gives a 70 Hz line as the strongest peak at 18.7 %. (5) The whine starts with an 8 ms rise from nothing; there is no contactor click at the start.

sounds.layers: Two channels from mid and side (synth.mid_side). Mid: pneumatic hiss, noise 3-9 kHz, 4 ms rise, 0.10 s hold, T60 0.07 s (audible 0-0.25 s), 4.5 %; servo growl from 70 rising to about 155 Hz (1.2 s smoothstep, 1.2 % wobble at 5.2 Hz), six harmonics, amplitude-modulated by 55 % low-passed noise and 25 % at 31 Hz, low-passed at 650 Hz, runs 0.14 to 1.84 s, 16 %; sweeping whine 300 to 900 Hz (then down 18 % before the slam) with harmonics 2 and 3, left and right detuned +-0.4 %, mid is the sum 10 %, side the difference 3.5 %; slam at 1.85 s: sub 70 falling to 35 Hz (tau 0.16 s, 4 ms rise, 0.08 s hold, T60 0.5 s) 27 %, thud noise 90-450 Hz (T60 0.16 s) 10 %, saturated crack 250-6000 Hz 4 % (side: 900-6000 Hz 1.5 %); metallic ring: 12 inharmonic partials from 230 Hz (ratios 1 to 13.6), detuned pairs, T60 0.95 s at 230 Hz and (230/f)^0.8 faster above, mid is the sum of the pair 14 %, side the difference 6 %, so each ear gets one member; last puff of air at 2.20 s, noise 2.5-7.5 kHz, 35 ms rise, 12 ms hold, T60 80 ms, 1.2 % plus 1.0 % side. Hiss side is independent noise 4.5 %.
sounds.measured: Hiss occupies 0-0.25 s at 3-9 kHz (the first 30 ms: centre 6.3 kHz, 100 % above 1 kHz). Growl and whine lines visible in the spectrogram; growl 70-155 Hz, whine 300-900 Hz sweeping up and bending down before the slam. Slam at 1.85 s with sub 70-35 Hz (20-90 Hz band -31 dBFS then -36, -48, -59 dBFS per 100 ms, i.e. still visible about 0.6 s). Ring: 200-4000 Hz band falls -31, -41, -50 dBFS over the first 300 ms and stays near -50 until the puff, so the metallic ring is about 0.4 to 0.5 s but 20 dB under the slam. Correlation 0.68 (0.3-0.9), level difference 0.31 dB, correlation below 150 Hz 0.9999, mono sum is the mid. Onset 0.9 ms, last 10 ms -93.7 dBFS. 2.6 s, true peak -10.1 dBFS, -35.0 LUFS.
sounds.unsure: (1) The ring is quiet next to the slam (about 20 dB under after 0.2 s); if it should be a defining feature, raise the ring share. (2) The growl is a stack of harmonics that shows as parallel horizontal lines; it may sound like a chord or organ drone rather than a servo growl, the 31 Hz and noise amplitude modulation are what make it rough. (3) Hiss and puff are close to identical in character; the puff comes 0.35 s after the slam, partly over the ring. (4) CLAP calls it 'an arcade video game sound effect' (margin -0.18, lowest after gear_c), probably the clean sweeping whine plus the hiss. (5) Low peak (-10.1 dBFS) follows the LUFS rule; its sub is under-weighted by K-weighting.

sounds.layers: One channel. Whine: fundamental 150 rising to 350 Hz over 0.8 s and holding, four harmonics (1, .85, .70, .50), wobble +-1.2 %, ratchet dips about 24 per second at depth 40 %, low-passed at 1.9 kHz (4th order), 50 % of energy; tooth ticks (900-2400 Hz, about 26 per second, low-passed 2.6 kHz) 4 %. Lock at 1.55 s: tick, noise 1-3 kHz low-passed 3 kHz, T60 7 ms, 8 %; 2 ms later the thunk: body noise 80-250 Hz (T60 0.10 s) 16 %, sub 80 falling to 52 Hz (T60 0.16 s) 12 %. No ring layer.
sounds.measured: 500 Hz-1.5 kHz share is at least 10 % (500-1000 Hz alone 21.6 %, 1-2 kHz 15.1 %); above 3 kHz 0.6 % (<=2); lock attack (30 ms): 23.6 % above 1 kHz (15-35); lock 300 ms: 26.9 % below 80 Hz (>=10), 33.0 % at 80-250 Hz, 0.7 % above 3 kHz. Whole file 21.6 % above 1 kHz. No ring: the sound is silent 0.15 s after the lock (the low sub tail is gone by 1.75 s). Onset 3.0 ms, last 10 ms -95.7 dBFS. 2.2 s, true peak -7.1 dBFS, -35.0 LUFS. CLAP margin -0.27, best 'a cheap electronic beep' (the whine is a clean tone with four harmonics).
sounds.unsure: (1) The whine is the loudest thing for 1.5 s and has no noise around it; CLAP hears a beep. It may sound like a synthesiser rather than a machine behind a wall. (2) The lock is short (thunk about 0.15 s) and the 'tick' spreads over 1-5 kHz in the spectrogram (the 4th-order low-pass at 3 kHz leaves only 0.6 % above 3 kHz overall but the tick edge is broad). (3) It has the highest sub-80 Hz share of the lock but little below 60 Hz overall (2.3 % of the file).

checks.name: build of the six ids
checks.result: all six pass the hard rules (peak, DC, onset, last 10 ms); clap-margin hint on five (only hull_c passes it). Integrated loudness hull a/b/c -31.0/-31.0/-31.0 LUFS, gear a/b/c -35.0/-35.0/-35.0 LUFS at true peaks -1.2/-11.1/-7.0 and -6.3/-10.1/-7.1 dBFS.

checks.name: unit tests of tools/audio/synth
checks.result: 45 tests OK, including the 9 new ones in test_pilot_mech.py (twice equal, shape, finite, peak, DC, onset, silent end, and key targets of every sound). The README command with -t tools/audio fails here with 'Start directory is not importable' for the existing tests as well; the plain command works.

checks.name: spectrogram pictures looked at
checks.result: Looked at all six. Hull a, b and gear b/c were re-read after the shares changed only for hull a; the rest are from the second-to-last tuning pass (shares unchanged afterwards except gear_b's ring T60/tilt and the final levels, whose numbers I re-measured).

checks.name: band shares, attack, lock windows, channel correlation
checks.command: scratch numpy script outside the repository (no window, mean removed) plus tools/audio/listen/measure.py
checks.result: numbers as in the per-sound entries; measure.py onset 0.02 to 3.7 ms for all six

checks.name: CLAP with the pilot negatives
checks.result: margins: hull_a -0.08 (best neg: taut plastic foil), hull_b -0.06 (taut plastic foil), hull_c +0.16 (ok), gear_a -0.05 (cheap electronic beep), gear_b -0.18 (arcade game sound), gear_c -0.27 (cheap electronic beep). The scores move by 0.03-0.05 between two renders of the same sound with different level or dither, so only large differences mean anything.

notVerified: Nothing was heard: all character claims (metal vs bowl, foil, tone vs machine, how large it sounds) are from numbers, spectrograms and CLAP only.
The Qwen describe model was not run (the brief forbids --describe).
No comparison against the reference files (k_hit_lowboom_0, impact_hull_medium.wav, gear_deploy.wav) was run beyond what SOUND_DESIGN.md already states; I did not measure them again.

The spectrogram of hull_b, hull_c and the three gear sounds was inspected on the second-to-last parameter set; after that I changed the plate share/tilt of hull a (re-inspected), the sub T60 of hull b, the ring of gear b, the hull_c knock/body edge and the levels, and re-measured their numbers but did not look at those pictures again.
Mono-sum, low-band equality and correlation are checked by number (0.49 and 0.68, bass correlation 1.0000 and 0.9999), not by listening on headphones.
The hull_a ring of 'at least 0.8 s' is met in the sense that partials ring the whole file, but its level at 0.8 s is about 57 dBFS RMS, so whether it is audible depends on the listening level.
The audition page and the manifest hash flow were not run; only build.py for my ids.
